canonical_question: How does the 1542 MPa value compare to theoretical predictions for this specific alloy system to validate the 'remarkable increase' claim?

question_variants.question: How does the 1542 MPa value compare to theoretical predictions for this specific alloy system to validate the 'remarkable increase' claim?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document provides the comparative experimental values (1542 MPa vs 1010 MPa) to support the claim of 'remarkable increase', but it does not provide theoretical predictions for the alloy system to validate the claim against theory, only against experimental data of the as-cast alloy.

answers.answer: Provides the baseline compressive strength of the as-cast alloy (1010 MPa) for comparison.
evidence_spans: Therefore, on the basis of design principles above, a new RHEA with equiatomic composition of NbMoCrTiAl was designed by B. Gorr et al. [ [13] , [14] ].
The as-cast alloy with low density (7.58 g/cm 3 ) exhibits excellent oxidation resistance.
The declining oxidation rate at 1100 °C was mainly due to the formation of Al, Cr-rich oxide layers.

answers.answer: Provides the composite strength value (1542 MPa) and the comparison to the as-cast value.
answers.processing_state: P/M composite with dispersed carbides and oxides
evidence_spans: In this work, in order to further increase the strength of NbMoCrTiAl RHEA, the P/M composite with dispersed carbides and oxides was developed through ball milling and spark plasma sintering (SPS) method.
The phase constitutions, microstructures, and mechanical properties of the NbMoCrTiAl HEA composite were investigated in detail.
